findings.summary: Arizona audit subcontractor details: Honey was employee of Wake TSI AND owner of Haystack Investigations — both worked on the audit. Wake TSI led initial hand-counting of ballots. Wake TSI had previously conducted partisan election review in Fulton County, PA. Gene Kern (Wake TSI) objected that Cyber Ninjas CEO Doug Logan took Honey and turned her from PE Director into floor manager without consulting Wake. Honey then attempted to recruit Wake TSI subcontractors to work for StratTech Solutions (the replacement firm). Wake TSI workers were billed at over $200/hour, with proposed daily rates reaching $2,400 for project directors. Wake declined to renew contract in mid-May 2021 after payment disputes. By May 23, agreement reached allowing Cyber Ninjas/StratTech to directly employ Wake's former workers.

PA Open Records case AP 2021-2612 (Honey and Haystack LLC v. PA Dept of State, filed Oct 2021, decided Dec 22, 2021): Honey requested list of voters who registered without an identification number, broken down by county and method of registration. Partially granted/partially denied. Agency argued some records governed by Voter Registration Act (denied) but failed to prove all requested records don't exist (granted). This was the data that Honey used for her 'more votes than voters' claims. Separately, Honey filed PA Dept of State complaint (Sept 2022) regarding overseas voter identification requirements; dismissed Nov 2022; appealed to Commonwealth Court.
